instagram.caption:
Stores use this psychology trick on you every single day ⚓

In a classic 1974 study, Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman spun a wheel rigged to land on 10 or 65, then asked an unrelated question; people who saw 65 gave much higher estimates. That first number becomes an anchor. 'Was' prices and opening offers work the same way.

Follow for more psychology that saves you money.
